translation_en: Ismail ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to me, from Muawiyah ibn Abi Muzarrid, from Sa‘id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Allah created creation, and when He had finished, the womb stood and said, ‘This is the standing of one seeking refuge in You from severing ties.’ He said, ‘Will you not be pleased that I maintain ties with whoever maintains you and sever ties with whoever severs you?’ It said, ‘Yes, my Lord.’ He said, ‘That is for you.’” Then Abu Hurayrah recited: “Would you then, if you were given authority, spread corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?” Quran 47:22.

Musaddad narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salih, from Ubaydullah, from Zayd ibn Khalid, who said: Rain fell upon the Prophet, and he said, “Some of My servants have entered the morning as disbelievers in Me and believers in Me.”

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Allah says, ‘When My servant loves to meet Me, I love to meet him; and when he dislikes meeting Me, I dislike meeting him.’”
Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu‘ayb informed us: Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Allah says, ‘I am as My servant thinks of Me.’”

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah said: “A man who had never done any good said, ‘When I die, burn me and scatter half of me on land and half in the sea. By Allah, if Allah gains power over me, He will punish me with a punishment with which He has punished no one among the worlds.’ Allah commanded the sea to gather what was in it and the land to gather what was in it. Then He said to him, ‘Why did you do that?’ He replied, ‘Out of fear of You, though You know best.’ So He forgave him.”

Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Amr ibn Asim narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Abdullah narrated to us: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah say: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Prophet say: “A servant committed a sin”—or he said, “did something sinful”—“and said, ‘My Lord, I have sinned’”—or, “I did wrong”—“so forgive me. His Lord said, ‘Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and punishes for them? I have forgiven My servant.’ Then he remained for as long as Allah willed and committed another sin—or did wrong—and said, ‘My Lord, I have sinned again, so forgive me.’ He said, ‘Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and punishes for them? I have forgiven My servant.’ Then he remained for as long as Allah willed and sinned again—or did wrong—and said, ‘My Lord, I have sinned again, so forgive me.’ He said, ‘Does My servant know that he has a Lord who forgives sins and punishes for them? I have forgiven My servant’”—three times—“so let him do as he wishes.”

Abdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us: I heard my father say: Qatadah narrated to us, from Uqbah ibn Abd al-Ghafir, from Abu Sa‘id, from the Prophet, who mentioned a man among those who came before you. He said that Allah had given the man wealth and children. When death approached, he said to his sons, “What kind of father have I been to you?” They said, “A good father.” He said, “But he has stored up no good with Allah, and if Allah gains power over him, He will punish him. So when I die, burn me until I become charcoal, then crush me”—or he said, “grind me”—“and when there is a stormy windy day, scatter me in it.” The Prophet of Allah said, “He made them swear by my Lord to do that. They did so and scattered him on a stormy day. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, ‘Be,’ and there he was, a man standing. Allah said, ‘My servant, what made you do what you did?’ He replied, ‘Fear of You,’ or, ‘dread of You.’ Nothing but His mercy then overtook him”—or on another occasion he said, “Nothing but that overtook him.” I related this to Abu Uthman, who said, “I heard this from Salman, except that he added: ‘Scatter me in the sea,’ or words to that effect.” Musa narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us and said “lam yabta’ir.” Khalifah narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us and said “lam yabta’iz.” Qatadah explained it as “he did not save up.”

Yusuf ibn Rashid narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Humayd, who said: I heard Anas say: I heard the Prophet say: “On the Day of Resurrection I will be granted intercession. I will say, ‘My Lord, admit to Paradise whoever has a mustard seed’s weight in his heart.’ They will enter. Then I will say, ‘Admit to Paradise whoever has even the least thing in his heart.’” Anas said: It is as though I can see the fingers of the Messenger of Allah.
